title: 8 ChatGPT Prompts for Social Media Content (2026)
description: An eight-step social content system that builds a month of platform-native posts from your core message — covering brand voice documentation, content calendar planning, per-platform copywriting for LinkedIn, Instagram, and X, and engagement follow-up — so you post consistently without burning out.
benefit: Go from 'I have no idea what to post' to a full month of on-brand social content in one session.

steps.title: Document your brand voice
steps.promptText:
Help me document a clear, consistent brand voice I can use to brief any AI tool for content creation.

My brand/business: [DESCRIBE IN 1–2 SENTENCES]
My audience: [WHO YOU'RE SPEAKING TO]
Examples of content I've published that felt 'right': [PASTE 2–3 EXAMPLES OR DESCRIBE THEM]

From this, define:
1. Tone descriptors: 3–5 adjectives that describe how I sound (not what I talk about)
2. 3 'sounds like us' examples — short phrases or sentences in my voice
3. 3 'doesn't sound like us' examples — phrases to avoid
4. My content promise: what can a follower expect to learn, feel, or get from following me?
5. A one-paragraph 'voice brief' I can paste into any future prompt to keep content on-brand
steps.whyThisTool: A voice brief created once and reused across every content prompt is the single highest-leverage investment in consistent social content — inconsistency is the #1 reason brand accounts stagnate.
steps.outputExpected: 5 tone descriptors, 3 on/off examples each, a content promise, and a reusable one-paragraph voice brief.

steps.title: Generate a month of content angles
steps.promptText:
Voice brief: [PASTE YOUR VOICE BRIEF FROM STEP 1]
Audience: [DESCRIBE]
Content goal this month: [e.g. grow LinkedIn following / drive traffic to blog / launch a product]

Generate 20 content angle ideas for this month. Rules:
- Each idea should be specific enough to write immediately (not 'share a tip about X' — 'the specific mistake most [audience] make when doing X')
- Cover 5 types: educational, story/personal, opinion/hot take, behind-the-scenes, promotional (4 of each)
- Rate each angle: relevance to audience / likely engagement / alignment with goal (1–5 each)
- Flag the 8 strongest angles I should use this month — the rest are a backlog
steps.whyThisTool: Planning angles by type (not just topic) ensures you're not accidentally posting 20 educational pieces in a row — which trains your audience to ignore you when you promote something.
steps.outputExpected: 20 specific content angles with type labels and 3-axis ratings, with the top 8 flagged for this month.

steps.title: Write a LinkedIn post that builds authority
steps.promptText:
Voice brief: [PASTE VOICE BRIEF]
Angle: [PICK ONE FROM STEP 2]

Write a LinkedIn post that builds professional authority. Format:
- Line 1: a bold claim or specific insight that makes someone stop scrolling — not 'I've been thinking about...' or 'Excited to share...'
- Body (150–300 words): develop the claim with one specific story, example, or data point
- Closing line: a specific takeaway or question the reader can engage with
- Line breaks every 2–3 sentences (LinkedIn readers skim)

Then write 3 alternative opening lines for A/B testing. Do not use: 'Unpopular opinion:', 'Hot take:', or 'This might be controversial but...'
steps.whyThisTool: The first line of a LinkedIn post determines whether the 'see more' button is clicked — writing three alternatives before picking one improves your hook quality more than any single rule.
steps.outputExpected: A full LinkedIn post with strong hook, developed argument, and engaging close — plus 3 alternative opening lines.

steps.title: Write an Instagram caption
steps.promptText:
Voice brief: [PASTE VOICE BRIEF]
Post type: [PHOTO / CAROUSEL / REEL]
Angle: [PICK ONE FROM STEP 2]

Write an Instagram caption:
- Hook (first line, 125 characters max): must work without seeing the image — grab attention with words alone
- Body (200–400 words): tell the story or share the insight — Instagram rewards length more than most marketers think
- CTA: one specific action (not 'follow me' — something actionable like 'save this', 'share to someone who needs this', or 'comment your answer below')
- Hashtags: 10 relevant hashtags at the end in 3 tiers: 3 niche (under 100k posts), 5 mid (100k–1M), 2 broad (1M+)

Also write the first comment I should post immediately after — algorithm signals help with early engagement.
steps.whyThisTool: Instagram captions with a clear mid-size hashtag strategy and an early comment still significantly outperform no-strategy posts — even as the algorithm evolves.
steps.outputExpected: A full Instagram caption with hook, body, CTA, tiered hashtags, and a suggested first comment for early engagement signaling.

steps.title: Write a Twitter/X thread with engagement hooks
steps.promptText:
Voice brief: [PASTE VOICE BRIEF]
Angle: [PICK ONE FROM STEP 2]

Write a Twitter/X thread (10–15 tweets):
- Tweet 1: hook — bold claim or counterintuitive fact. No 'Thread:' label. No '1/'.
- Tweets 2–12: each standalone — a reader who sees only this tweet should find it interesting without context
- Include 2 're-engagement tweets' at tweets 5 and 10: these are recap tweets that also serve as standalone insights for people joining mid-thread
- Final tweet: a clear CTA (follow, reply, save, or click a link)
- Under each tweet, rate engagement potential: HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW based on how shareable it is as a standalone

Max 240 chars per tweet. Number them.
steps.whyThisTool: Re-engagement tweets at positions 5 and 10 address thread drop-off — the readers who scroll past tweets 2–4 can re-enter at a re-engagement tweet and still understand what's happening.
steps.outputExpected: 10–15 numbered tweets with re-engagement hooks at positions 5 and 10, per-tweet engagement ratings, and a CTA final tweet.

steps.title: Build a 30-day posting calendar
steps.promptText:
Using the 8 priority angles from Step 2 and the platform formats from Steps 3–5, build a 30-day social media calendar.

Platforms I post to: [LIST: e.g. LinkedIn, Instagram, X]
Posting frequency per platform: [e.g. LinkedIn 3x/week, Instagram 5x/week, X daily]

Calendar requirements:
- Vary content types (educational / story / opinion / promotional) — don't post the same type twice in a row
- Promotional content: max 20% of posts
- Platform-native format for each post (not the same content cross-posted)
- Flag 3 dates this month that are high-engagement windows: Tue–Thu mornings for LinkedIn, Fri evenings for Instagram, etc.
- Format: Day | Platform | Angle | Content type | Format (post/thread/carousel/reel)
steps.whyThisTool: Variety in content type is the most underrated posting strategy — an all-educational feed trains followers to come for information and tune out anything that looks promotional.
steps.outputExpected: A 30-day calendar table with day, platform, angle, content type, and format — varied by type, with high-engagement window flags.

steps.title: Write engagement replies at scale
steps.promptText:
I need to reply to comments on my posts to boost engagement and build community. Here are 10 comments from my recent posts:

[PASTE COMMENTS]

For each comment, write a reply that:
- Acknowledges the specific thing they said (not 'Great point!' as an opener)
- Adds one new piece of value or perspective — doesn't just say thank you
- Ends with a question that keeps the conversation going
- Matches my brand voice: [PASTE VOICE BRIEF]

Also flag any comment that is a potential customer question — these deserve a longer, separate response.
steps.whyThisTool: Replies that add value (not just 'Thanks!') significantly boost comment thread depth, which is a key algorithmic signal on LinkedIn and Instagram. The 'add one new thing' rule is the constraint that makes this work.
steps.outputExpected: 10 value-adding replies in your brand voice, each ending with a conversation-continuing question, plus customer-inquiry flags.

steps.title: Analyze what's working and iterate
steps.promptText:
Here are my social media metrics for the last month:

[PASTE: views / likes / comments / shares / profile clicks / follows per post — or describe your top and bottom performers]

Analyze what's working:
1. What content types, angles, or formats performed best — what pattern explains the top 3 posts?
2. What content types consistently underperformed — should I stop creating these?
3. What's my best performing opening line or hook format? What should I replicate?
4. What content topic gets the most comments vs. the most shares? These are different engagement signals.
5. Based on this data, recommend 3 changes to my content strategy for next month: one to do more of, one to do less of, one to test for the first time
steps.whyThisTool: Analyzing top vs. bottom performers for patterns (not just volume) is how content strategy improves over time rather than just producing more of the same thing.
steps.outputExpected: A pattern analysis of top/bottom performers, hook format recommendation, comments-vs-shares signal breakdown, and 3 concrete strategy adjustments for next month.

faq.q: Can I use the same content on every platform?
faq.a: No — and that's the point of Steps 3–5. LinkedIn, Instagram, and X have different audiences, different algorithmic behaviors, and different native formats. Cross-posting the same text verbatim is one of the clearest signals that a brand doesn't understand their platforms.

faq.q: How much time does this 8-step system take?
faq.a: Step 1 (voice brief) is a one-time 20-minute investment. Steps 2 and 6 (angles + calendar) take about an hour at the start of each month. Steps 3–5 (individual post copy) take 10–15 minutes per post with this system vs. 30–60 minutes from scratch.

faq.q: Will the AI-written posts sound authentic?
faq.a: Only if you use the voice brief correctly. Pasting a generic voice brief produces generic content. The more specific you make the voice brief in Step 1 — including real examples of your writing — the more on-brand the output will be. Treat it as a briefing document, not a shortcut.
